description: Add the workspace's receiving domain: a domain or subdomain whose mail should reach the inbox. Once verified, replies to emails from all sending domains use reply addresses on it. Then the user publishes the returned MX record (and TXT record when listed) and you call verify_receiving_domain; the first verification turns Inbox on. A workspace has one receiving domain: a second returns 409 limit_reached before any DNS check (remove the current one first, after confirming with the user). A domain that already receives email elsewhere (its MX points at Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Cloudflare Email Routing...) returns 409 domain_has_mailbox: suggest a subdomain such as support.acme.com and confirm with the user. 503 dns_check_failed means the MX lookup got no answer; retry in a minute. created is false when the workspace already has the name (returned unchanged, no check). The first receiving domain also sets replyTrackingDomainMode custom. Owner or admin only.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

domain.description: Domain or subdomain to receive on, e.g. support.acme.com.

name: add_receiving_domain

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `add_receiving_domain` MCP tool.

created.description: True when the domain was added; false when the company already had it.

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: Human-readable status, confirmation, or next-step message.

receivingDomain.description: Receiving domain {id, domain, status (verified|pending|failed), records [{type MX|TXT, name, value, priority?, status}] to publish, error, claimExpiresAt (when an unverified name stops being reserved), verifiedAt, lastCheckedAt, createdAt}.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.
